title: Rare-earth magnet chain

chokepoint.physics: Solvent-extraction separation of chemically-alike elements — an industrial base, ~91% China

eyebrow: Product-chain pilot · the motors that move everything
h1: The mine is the least of it — China's grip tightens downstream
deck: Rare-earth permanent magnets turn EV motors, wind generators and guided weapons. Everyone points at the mine, where China holds ~60%. But the real chokepoint is the separation plant — and China's share does not fall along the chain, it climbs: ~91% of separation, ~94% of the finished magnets.
byline: mine (~60%) ≠ separation & refining (~91%) ≠ sintered NdFeB magnet (~94%) ≠ the motor
correction: Opening a rare-earth mine in Australia or the United States does little on its own, because the ore still has to be chemically separated — and separation is ~91% China, magnet-making ~94% China. The chokepoint is not the deposit; it is the refinery and the magnet plant downstream of it, and China's hold gets stronger at each step rather than weaker.

history.title: The chokepoint deepened: China's magnet share, 2005 → 2024
history.note: IEA. Two published anchors — China made roughly half the world's sintered permanent magnets around 2005 and about 94% by 2024 — not an annual interpolated series, so it is marked as an estimate. The line the atlas keeps finding is here in its starkest form: as capability moved downstream, the concentration did not dilute, it intensified.

hops.t: ore carrying many rare-earth elements — China ~60%, plus the US, Myanmar, Australia
solvent-extraction splits 15+ chemically-alike elements into oxides — ~91% China
reduce to metal, cast NdFeB alloy strip
press, sinter, machine, coat, magnetise — ~94% China

sections.h2: 1 · The chokepoint moves downstream — and deepens

panels.h3: China's share along the magnet chain (2024)
panels.note: IEA, magnet-specific physical stages. The single most important shape in this chain: the bars go UP, not down. Most supply worries fixate on the mine, where China is 'only' ~60%. Every step after it is more concentrated, not less.

panels.h3: Why separation is the hard step
panels.text: Rare earths are not rare in the ground; they are rare as separated, high-purity oxides. The elements are chemically almost identical, so pulling them apart takes long cascades of solvent-extraction stages, large reagent flows and the environmental permitting that comes with them. That industrial base — not the ore body — is what sits ~91% in China, and it is what a new mine elsewhere does not replace.

sections.h2: 2 · The heavies are the real scarcity

panels.text: Neodymium and praseodymium give NdFeB magnets their strength; dysprosium and terbium — the 'heavy' rare earths — let them keep that strength hot, in a traction motor or a missile fin. The heavies are geologically scarcer and their separation is even more concentrated in China than the lights, so the part of the magnet that matters most for high-temperature and defence use is the part with the thinnest alternative supply.
panels.note: IEA / USGS: Dy and Tb are the binding heavy-rare-earth constraint.

panels.h3: Substitution is partial, not a way out
panels.text: Ferrite and other magnet chemistries exist and are used where performance allows, and engineers trim dysprosium with grain-boundary diffusion. But for the power-dense motors that electrification and defence actually want, NdFeB with some heavies remains the material — so the dependence persists even as the hedges are researched.

sections.h2: 3 · The lever has already been pulled

panels.h3: From technology ban to export licensing
panels.text: China banned the export of its rare-earth extraction, separation and magnet-making technology in December 2023, then in April 2025 placed several medium and heavy rare earths and their magnets under export licensing — briefly throttling shipments to Western automakers and defence suppliers. It is the same playbook the atlas documents for gallium, germanium and antimony: a downstream chokepoint, turned into a policy instrument.
panels.flag: the same export-control playbook (see the defence chain)

trade_intro: BACI carries rare-earth compounds and permanent magnets (HS 850511), but customs origin is the last shipment point, not where the ore was separated — magnets assembled into a motor cross as the motor. Read the export shares below as trading positions, not the separation map, which is the real chokepoint and is not visible in trade.
